input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: The duplicate-numbered § 12.4 (p0046) imposes a post-term, all-territory competitive ban on Customer for twenty-four months with no carve-outs — walk-away territory and a failure of the fallback on scope, duration and carve-outs. It also contradicts § 12.3 (p0044), where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. The smallest operative cure is flipping the prohibitory operator ("shall not" to "may"), which leaves no non-compete and no field-of-use or territorial restriction on Customer, consistent with the preferred position. The no-hire covenant at p0045 is left to the applicable rule.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept any restriction on the products or services we develop, buy or sell, so we have flipped the prohibitory operator in the second § 12.4 to a permission, which also cures the direct contradiction with § 12.3. If Cobalt needs protection, we could consider a narrow term-only restriction on a single named competing product, capped at 12 months with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Convert the 24-month, all-territory non-compete on Customer into an express permission.
